# Gate current sanity check

## What
A sanity check at the start of a cooldown: sweep each active gate from 0 out
to each of its previously established card limits (others parked at 0),
watching gate current at pA resolution — does it leak, or does it look safe?
Safe → move on. Leaks → stop and report. Not a leakage test; a quick
liveness-and-gross-safety pass before the campaign starts.

## When
Once per cooldown, after instrument init and the measurement-config block,
before any subsequent recipe. Optionally also after thermal cycling or
physical intervention (reseating contacts, swapping a bias source).

**Preconditions:**
- Card-provided gate limits exist (device card, or a prior `gate-range-finding`).
- Gates ungrounded, device in a measurable configuration.

## Why
This is the cooldown's liveness check, run before any measurement because
everything downstream assumes it holds: the device is alive — passes a
measurable current — and every gate stays clean across the range the campaign
will use. The gate validators are already committed (the gate-validators slot,
from the card); this check confirms the device is actually safe within them. A
gate that leaks within its range is a data and device-safety problem. This is
a liveness and gross-safety check, not a leakage test: characterizing a
leakage onset is `gate-leakage-survey`, re-deriving the range is
`gate-range-finding`.

## Recipe

Two cells. HERA proposes both together. The human runs Cell A once — it loops
every leg (each gate × both polarities), each leg getting its own file and
slug — watching the live gate-current plot, then runs Cell B once. No
copy-the-cell iteration: the legs are enumerated up front.

### Cell A — gate sweep

Sweeps every active gate from 0 to each of its card limits, other gates
parked at 0. `nplci=10` on the gate-current channels for high-SNR pA
readback (~167 ms/pt); it stays at 10 across the sweep, Cell B resets it.

```python
# === Gate sweep: every active gate, 0 -> each of its card limits ===
# Endpoints = the device-card gate limits set as TG_MIN/TG_MAX, BG_MIN/BG_MAX in the
# gate-validators slot. Nothing to hand-substitute.
# Watch the live gate-current plot per leg: pA, riding the charging slope = safe.
# A gross turn-up off that slope = it's leaking -> Kernel Interrupt (the try/finally
# parks the gate); stop and report (skip Cell B).

# one leg per gate per polarity, (gate, endpoint)
legs = [
    (k_tg, TG_MAX), (k_tg, TG_MIN),
    (k_bg, BG_MAX), (k_bg, BG_MIN),
]
n_pts   = 251
delay   = 1            # s
lockins = [sr830_1, sr830_2, sr830_3, sr830_4]   # match your mc

# pA-floor readback on the gate-current channels; Cell B resets to 1.
k_tg.nplci(10)
k_bg.nplci(10)

# AC sense drive ~1 nA (liveness current) via the device-card drive->current relation
# — don't inherit the lock-in's residual amplitude (it starves the X read).
sr830_1.amplitude(<amp for ~1 nA per device card>)

for gate, v_endpoint in legs:
    s = sweep.AsyncStation(measurement_config)
    s.add_comment('gate-current-sanity-check')
    s.add_comment(f'gate: {gate.name}')
    s.add_comment(f'leg: 0 -> {v_endpoint:+g} V (card limit)')

    # park gates at 0 (the swept one starts from 0)
    s.ramp(k_tg.volt, 0)
    s.ramp(k_bg.volt, 0)

    xp = gate.volt
    other = k_bg if gate is k_tg else k_tg
    # temperature: fp it per the rig card's polling rules
    # The swept gate's V is already the sweep's setpoint column — re-fp'ing it
    # writes a duplicate column name. fp the held gate's V + both currents.
    s.fp(other.volt)
    s.fp(gate.curr).fp(other.curr)
    s.plot(xp, k_tg.curr)
    s.plot(xp, k_bg.curr)
    for lia in lockins:
        s.fp(lia.X).fp(lia.P)
        s.plot(xp, lia.X)

    try:
        s.sweep(gate.volt, np.linspace(0, v_endpoint, n_pts), delay=delay)
    finally:
        s.ramp(gate.volt, 0)

Each leg's endpoint is a device-card gate limit — the `TG_MIN/TG_MAX`,
`BG_MIN/BG_MAX` set in the gate-validators slot — so there are no limit numbers
to hand-substitute; HERA just lists the legs. The `lockins` list should match
the channels in your `measurement_config`; if `mc` lists exactly the active
sr830s HERA may pre-fill it, otherwise the human sets it.

Read the live plot per leg:
- Lock-in `X`: nonzero, smoothly varying → device alive.
- Swept gate `*.curr`: stays in pA, on the capacitive charging slope, to the
  limit → safe.
- Parked gate `*.curr`: at the readback floor → no cross-gate path.

A geometry-derived ceiling (≈ ±0.5 V/nm × hBN thickness for the metal gates)
sanity-checks the card limits themselves: if a card limit exceeds it, treat
the card as suspect — don't sweep to it, flag to the operator before running.

### Cell B — reset nplci

After every leg has run, reset gate-current `nplci` back to standard. Only run
this if every leg looked safe; if anything leaked, stop and report instead (a
leaking gate is `gate-leakage-survey`'s problem, not this recipe's).

```python
# === Reset gate-current nplci ===
# Validators were already committed in the gate-validators slot — nothing to re-commit.
# Undo Cell A's nplci bump; print the live validators to confirm.
k_tg.nplci(1)
k_bg.nplci(1)

print("k_tg.volt validator:", k_tg.volt.vals)
print("k_bg.volt validator:", k_bg.volt.vals)
```

### HERA handshake

HERA proposes Cell A (all legs) and Cell B together, and **does not propose
any subsequent recipe step until the human reports the per-leg results.** If
everything looked safe HERA moves on; if any gate leaked HERA stops and
reports — it never advances on a gate that leaked. Human is the gate; HERA
waits.

### Failure-mode catalog

| What you see on the live plot | What it means | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Lock-in `X` nonzero and smoothly varying | Device alive, contact wiring good | Continue |
| Lock-in `X` flat zero on one channel | Wiring break on that contact pair | Stop; check wiring |
| Lock-in `X` flat-nonzero, **all channels at the same value** | Device tied to ground (shared-node short) — false signal that mimics readback | Stop; unground the device, then re-run Cell A |
| `k_*.curr` saturated at full-range readback (e.g. ±1 µA on `rangei=1e-6`) | Range too coarse for the leakage scale, or a real leak that pinned the range | Drop `rangei` to `1e-9` and re-run; if still saturated, real leak |
| `k_*.curr` makes a gross turn-up off the capacitive charging slope | It's leaking | Interrupt; stop and report (don't run Cell B); `gate-leakage-survey` to characterize |
| Parked gate `*.curr` tracks the swept gate | Cross-gate leakage path | Stop; characterize via `gate-leakage-survey` |

## Examples

- `aaron/RPL_10/241207_measure.ipynb` cells 22–25 — an early one-shot
  liveness check: three small fixed `0 → +1 V` sweeps (TG, BG, Si BG),
  full-range sweeps deferred to separate per-gate recipes. The canonical
  liveness shape; the loop here generalizes it to the card limits.
- `isaac/b1c2_toploader/20260505_measure.ipynb` cells 17–27 — first live
  HERA test, an early version of this recipe in action. Cell 22 is the sweep cell with
  `nplci=10` (using the older save/restore pattern). Hit the grounded-device
  failure mode (cell 26 diagnoses: sr830_2/3/4 share contact 30, all locked
  to ground potential). After ungrounding, manual range-finding established
  `k_tg.volt = (-7, +6)` and `k_bg.volt = (-4, +4.4)`; cell 27 commits the
  validators. The session also surfaced that `KEITHLEY_DEFAULTS["rangei"]`
  should be `1e-9` for pA-resolution; the b1c2 template was patched
  in-session.

## Next

- **Safe**: move on to the campaign's next recipe — every gate swept clean to
  its card limit on each side, and the `add_comment` slug captured the recipe
  identity in metadata.
- **Leaks**: stop and report; the operator decides whether to characterize via
  `gate-leakage-survey` or re-derive limits via `gate-range-finding`.
- **Results not reported**: HERA will not advance.

from qcodes import VisaInstrument

class Lakeshore_335(VisaInstrument):
    # TODO: PID.
    def __init__(self, name, address, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(name, address, terminator='\r\n', **kwargs)
        self.add_parameter('sample_temperature', get_cmd='KRDG? A', get_parser=float, unit='K')
        self.add_parameter('vaporizer_temperature', get_cmd='KRDG? B', get_parser=float, unit='K')
        self.add_parameter('sample_setpoint', get_cmd='SETP? 1', get_parser=float, set_cmd='SETP 1,{:.4f}', unit='K')
        self.add_parameter('vaporizer_setpoint', get_cmd='SETP? 2', get_parser=float, set_cmd='SETP 2,{:.4f}', unit='K')
        self.add_parameter('sample_range', get_cmd='RANGE? 1', get_parser=int, set_cmd='RANGE 1,{}')
        self.add_parameter('vaporizer_range', get_cmd='RANGE? 2', get_parser=int, set_cmd='RANGE 2,{}')
        self.add_parameter('sample_power', get_cmd = 'HTR? 1', get_parser=float, set_cmd = 'OUTMODE 1,3,0,0 \r\n MOUT 1,{:.4f}', unit='%')
        self.add_parameter('vaporizer_power', get_cmd = 'HTR? 2', get_parser=float, set_cmd = 'OUTMODE 2,3,0,0 \r\n MOUT 2,{:.4f}', unit='%')
        self.add_function('set_sample_closed_loop', call_cmd = 'OUTMODE 1,1,1,0')
        self.add_function('set_vaporizer_closed_loop', call_cmd = 'OUTMODE 2,1,2,0')
        #TODO: add ramp bool command        
        self.connect_message()
        
    def off(self, heater='both'):
        if heater=='sample':
            self.sample_range(0)
        elif heater=='vaporizer':
            self.vaporizer_range(0)
        elif heater=='both':
            self.sample_range(0)
            self.vaporizer_range(0)
        else:
            print(f'Error: Unknown heater type {heater}')
    
    def set_both(self, temperature, ratio=1):
        self.sample_setpoint(temperature)
        self.vaporizer_setpoint(temperature * ratio)
        r = 3
        if temperature < 20:
            r = 1
        elif temperature < 100:
            r = 2
        self.sample_range(r)
        self.vaporizer_range(r)

    def warmup(self):
        self.sample_setpoint(300)
        self.vaporizer_setpoint(100)
        self.sample_range(3)
        self.vaporizer_range(3)

# -------------------------------
    # User functions
    # -------------------------------
    def output_enabled(self) -> bool:
        """True if the supply output stage is on (OUT:?). Read-only."""
        return self._ask_value("OUT:?", "#OUT:") == "ON"

    def persistent_switch_on(self) -> bool:
        """True if the persistent-switch heater is energized (SWITCH:PERSISTENT:?). Read-only."""
        ps_state = self._ask_value("SWITCH:PERSISTENT:?", "#SWITCH:PERSISTENT:").upper()
        return "ENAB" in ps_state

    def _status(self) -> dict:
        """
        Query magnet/supply status; returns a dict of values.
        """
        output_enabled = self.output_enabled()
        persistent_on = self.persistent_switch_on()

        loop_mode = self._ask_value("LOOP:?", "#LOOP:")
        update_mode = self._ask_value("UPMODE:?", "#UPMODE:")
        field   = float(self._ask_value("GET:I:?", "#GET:I:")) * self.T_per_A
        voltage = float(self._ask_value("GET:V:?", "#GET:V:"))

        status_dict = {
            "voltage": voltage,
            "field": field,
            "output_enabled": output_enabled,
            "persistent_switch_on": persistent_on,
            "loop_mode": loop_mode,
            "update_mode": update_mode,
        }
        return status_dict

    def status(self) -> None:
        s = self._status()
        print("---------- Magnet Status ----------")
        print(f"Field:               : {s['field']:.3f} Tesla")
        print(f"Current:             : {s['field'] / self.T_per_A:.3f} A")
        print(f"Voltage:             : {s['voltage']:.3f} V")
        print(f"Output Enabled       : {s['output_enabled']}")
        print(f"Persistent Switch On : {s['persistent_switch_on']}")
        print(f"Loop Mode            : {s['loop_mode']}")
        print(f"Update Mode          : {s['update_mode']}")
        print("-----------------------------------")

    def heater_on(self) -> None:
        """
        Turn on persistent switch heater.
        (Supply command is SWITCH:PERSISTENT:ENABLE.)
        """
        self._write("SWITCH:PERSISTENT:ENABLE")
        time.sleep(10)

    def heater_off(self) -> None:
        """
        Turn off persistent switch heater.
        """
        self._write("SWITCH:PERSISTENT:DISABLE")
        time.sleep(10)

    def _is_ramping(self) -> bool:
        status_hex = self._ask_value("REG:STATUS:?", "#REG:STATUS:")
        status = int(status_hex, 16)
        return bool((status >> 21) & 1)

    def _get_field(self) -> float:
        """Measured field in Tesla: averaged current readback x T_per_A."""
        return float(self._ask_value("GET:I:?", "#GET:I:")) * self.T_per_A

    @property
    def commanded_field(self) -> float | None:
        """Last field target (Tesla) commanded via this driver, or None before
        any ramp this session. The supply does not expose its commanded
        set-point; this is the value stashed at issue. Reliable because the
        driver is the only ramp path — compare against the measured `field()`."""
        return self._ramp_target

    # -------------------------------

1	# `sweep` (measureme) API Reference
2	
3	The measurement layer: `lib/measureme`, imported as `import sweep`. A
4	`Station` collects QCoDeS parameters to follow, runs 0D–2D sweeps, and writes
5	each run to a directory (`data.tsv.gz` + `metadata.json`) via a `Writer`.
6	
7	Source: `sweep/sweep.py`, `sweep/db.py`. `import sweep` re-exports the
8	`sweep.sweep` surface (`from .sweep import *`); `sweep.db`, `sweep.raster`,
9	`sweep.sweep_load` are submodules.
10	
11	---
12	
13	## Station
14	
15	### `Station(measurement_config=None, basedir=None, verbose=True)`
16	A collection of followed parameters with sweep methods. `measurement_config`
17	is an arbitrary dict stamped into every run's `metadata.json` (channel→contact,
18	gains, bias, …). `basedir` is the run-directory root; falls back to the module
19	`BASEDIR` (see `set_basedir`) then `os.getcwd()`. The station writes `log.log`
20	into `basedir`, so the directory must exist before construction.
21	
22	### `AsyncStation(measurement_config=None, basedir=None, verbose=True)`
23	Subclass of `Station`, same constructor and identical I/O / data layout. Reads
24	are parallelized per-instrument (one thread per distinct instrument, one
25	executor reused across a sweep), and same-instrument parameters are
26	batch-read when supported — SR830 `snap` (`SnapReadable`, ≤6 params) or
27	SR86x `get_values` (`BatchReadable`, ≤3 params), else sequential. Use this by
28	default; it produces byte-identical output to `Station`.
29	
30	### `follow_param(param, gain=1.0)` → `Station` · alias **`fp`**
31	Append a QCoDeS parameter to the followed list. The stored column value is
32	**`param() / gain`** (gain division happens at read time). Returns the station,
33	so calls chain: `s.fp(sr0.X, gain).fp(sr0.P)`. For a true-current channel
34	follow it with `gain=1`. Column name is `param.full_name`.
35	
36	### `add_comment(comment)`
37	Append a comment to `metadata['comments']`. **Comments are station-lifetime**:
38	every comment added since construction lands in every subsequent run's
39	metadata — rebuild (or otherwise reset) the station between runs of different
40	intent. `metadata['comments'][0]` is conventionally the recipe slug.
41	
42	### `ramp(param, setpoint)`
43	Logged direct set — calls `param(setpoint)`. It does **not** sub-step; smooth
44	ramping is the driver's own `step`/`inter_delay` (or a driver `ramp_*` method).
45	
46	### `register_run_before(fn, args)` / `register_run_after(fn, args)`
47	Register a hook called at each measured point. `args` must be a tuple. The hook
48	is called `fn(*args, **context)` where **context is injected by parameter
49	name** (via `inspect.signature` — the hook receives only the context keys it
50	declares):
51	
52	| context key | available in | value |
53	|---|---|---|
54	| `station` | before & after | the `Station` |
55	| `writer` | before & after | the active `sweep.db.Writer` |
56	| `data` | after only | the most recent data row (list) |
57	
58	A hook whose parameter is named `station` gets it from context — passing it in
59	`args` too double-binds (`TypeError: multiple values for 'station'`). Order any
60	`args`-supplied params before the context ones. Keyword-only hook params can't
61	be set positionally via `args`; bind them with `functools.partial` (signature
62	is seen through the partial, so injection still works).
63	
64	### Other methods
65	- `measure()` → `SweepResult` — single 0D point.
66	- `watch(delay=0.0, max_duration=None)` → `SweepResult` — repeat-measure over
67	  time until `max_duration` (or interrupt).
68	- `read(param, gain=1.0)` / `read_all()` — log a one-off read, no run written.
69	- `plot(x, y, z=None)` / `reset_plots()` — live monitor only, not the data.
70	- `reset()` — clear the interrupted flag so the station can sweep again.
71	
72	---
73	
74	## Sweeps
75	
76	Each sweep method returns a `SweepResult` and writes one run directory. The
77	**data-row column layout** is fixed per method (and matches `metadata['columns']`).
78	`*followed` is the followed-parameter values in `fp` order, each already
79	gain-divided.
80	
81	| method | signature | row layout |
82	|---|---|---|
83	| `measure` | `()` | `[time, *followed]` |
84	| `watch` | `(delay=0.0, max_duration=None)` | `[time, *followed]` |
85	| `sweep` | `(param, setpoints, delay=0.0)` | `[time, setpoint, *followed]` |
86	| `multisweep` | `(params, setpointslist, delay=0.0)` | `[time, *setpoints, *followed]` |
87	| `megasweep` | `(slow_param, slow_v, fast_param, fast_v, slow_delay=0.0, fast_delay=0.0, init_delay=True)` | `[time, slow, fast, *followed]` |
88	| `multimegasweep` | `(slow_params, slow_v_list, fast_params, fast_v_list, slow_delay=0.0, fast_delay=0.0, init_delay=True)` | `[time, *slow, *fast, *followed]` |
89	
90	- **`sweep`** — 1D. Sets `param` to each setpoint, waits `delay`, measures.
91	- **`multisweep`** — 1D, several parameters **co-swept**. `params` and
92	  `setpointslist` are parallel lists; `setpointslist[i]` is the vector for
93	  `params[i]`, and **all vectors must be equal length** (raises otherwise). At
94	  point j every `params[i]` is set to `setpointslist[i][j]` — one path through
95	  N-space, not a grid (e.g. a fixed-D (Vtg, Vbg) line).
96	- **`megasweep`** — 2D grid: outer `slow_param` over `slow_v`, inner
97	  `fast_param` over `fast_v`. `slow_delay` waits once per slow row (at the first
98	  fast point), `fast_delay` waits at every point.
99	- **`multimegasweep`** — 2D grid where each axis is a **co-swept bundle**.
100	  `slow_params`/`slow_v_list` and `fast_params`/`fast_v_list` are parallel
101	  lists; per-axis all vectors must be equal length. The grid is
102	  `len(slow_v) × len(fast_v)`; at each grid point every slow param and every
103	  fast param is set together. Example — field-slow, (Vtg, Vbg)-line-fast:
104	  `s.multimegasweep([magnet.field], [B_vec], [k_tg.volt, k_bg.volt], [Vtgs, Vbgs], slow_delay=1, fast_delay=0.9)`.
105	- **`init_delay`** (2D only) — `True` applies `slow_delay` before the very

# `sweep` (measureme) API Reference

The measurement layer: `lib/measureme`, imported as `import sweep`. A
`Station` collects QCoDeS parameters to follow, runs 0D–2D sweeps, and writes
each run to a directory (`data.tsv.gz` + `metadata.json`) via a `Writer`.

Source: `sweep/sweep.py`, `sweep/db.py`. `import sweep` re-exports the
`sweep.sweep` surface (`from .sweep import *`); `sweep.db`, `sweep.raster`,
`sweep.sweep_load` are submodules.

---

## Station

### `Station(measurement_config=None, basedir=None, verbose=True)`
A collection of followed parameters with sweep methods. `measurement_config`
is an arbitrary dict stamped into every run's `metadata.json` (channel→contact,
gains, bias, …). `basedir` is the run-directory root; falls back to the module
`BASEDIR` (see `set_basedir`) then `os.getcwd()`. The station writes `log.log`
into `basedir`, so the directory must exist before construction.

### `AsyncStation(measurement_config=None, basedir=None, verbose=True)`
Subclass of `Station`, same constructor and identical I/O / data layout. Reads
are parallelized per-instrument (one thread per distinct instrument, one
executor reused across a sweep), and same-instrument parameters are
batch-read when supported — SR830 `snap` (`SnapReadable`, ≤6 params) or
SR86x `get_values` (`BatchReadable`, ≤3 params), else sequential. Use this by
default; it produces byte-identical output to `Station`.

### `follow_param(param, gain=1.0)` → `Station` · alias **`fp`**
Append a QCoDeS parameter to the followed list. The stored column value is
**`param() / gain`** (gain division happens at read time). Returns the station,
so calls chain: `s.fp(sr0.X, gain).fp(sr0.P)`. For a true-current channel
follow it with `gain=1`. Column name is `param.full_name`.

### `add_comment(comment)`
Append a comment to `metadata['comments']`. **Comments are station-lifetime**:
every comment added since construction lands in every subsequent run's
metadata — rebuild (or otherwise reset) the station between runs of different
intent. `metadata['comments'][0]` is conventionally the recipe slug.

### `ramp(param, setpoint)`
Logged direct set — calls `param(setpoint)`. It does **not** sub-step; smooth
ramping is the driver's own `step`/`inter_delay` (or a driver `ramp_*` method).

### `register_run_before(fn, args)` / `register_run_after(fn, args)`
Register a hook called at each measured point. `args` must be a tuple. The hook
is called `fn(*args, **context)` where **context is injected by parameter
name** (via `inspect.signature` — the hook receives only the context keys it
declares):

| context key | available in | value |
|---|---|---|
| `station` | before & after | the `Station` |
| `writer` | before & after | the active `sweep.db.Writer` |
| `data` | after only | the most recent data row (list) |

A hook whose parameter is named `station` gets it from context — passing it in
`args` too double-binds (`TypeError: multiple values for 'station'`). Order any
`args`-supplied params before the context ones. Keyword-only hook params can't
be set positionally via `args`; bind them with `functools.partial` (signature
is seen through the partial, so injection still works).

### Other methods
- `measure()` → `SweepResult` — single 0D point.
- `watch(delay=0.0, max_duration=None)` → `SweepResult` — repeat-measure over
  time until `max_duration` (or interrupt).
- `read(param, gain=1.0)` / `read_all()` — log a one-off read, no run written.
- `plot(x, y, z=None)` / `reset_plots()` — live monitor only, not the data.
- `reset()` — clear the interrupted flag so the station can sweep again.

---

## Sweeps

Each sweep method returns a `SweepResult` and writes one run directory. The
**data-row column layout** is fixed per method (and matches `metadata['columns']`).
`*followed` is the followed-parameter values in `fp` order, each already
gain-divided.

| method | signature | row layout |
|---|---|---|
| `measure` | `()` | `[time, *followed]` |
| `watch` | `(delay=0.0, max_duration=None)` | `[time, *followed]` |
| `sweep` | `(param, setpoints, delay=0.0)` | `[time, setpoint, *followed]` |
| `multisweep` | `(params, setpointslist, delay=0.0)` | `[time, *setpoints, *followed]` |
| `megasweep` | `(slow_param, slow_v, fast_param, fast_v, slow_delay=0.0, fast_delay=0.0, init_delay=True)` | `[time, slow, fast, *followed]` |
| `multimegasweep` | `(slow_params, slow_v_list, fast_params, fast_v_list, slow_delay=0.0, fast_delay=0.0, init_delay=True)` | `[time, *slow, *fast, *followed]` |

- **`sweep`** — 1D. Sets `param` to each setpoint, waits `delay`, measures.
- **`multisweep`** — 1D, several parameters **co-swept**. `params` and
  `setpointslist` are parallel lists; `setpointslist[i]` is the vector for
  `params[i]`, and **all vectors must be equal length** (raises otherwise). At
  point j every `params[i]` is set to `setpointslist[i][j]` — one path through
  N-space, not a grid (e.g. a fixed-D (Vtg, Vbg) line).
- **`megasweep`** — 2D grid: outer `slow_param` over `slow_v`, inner
  `fast_param` over `fast_v`. `slow_delay` waits once per slow row (at the first
  fast point), `fast_delay` waits at every point.
- **`multimegasweep`** — 2D grid where each axis is a **co-swept bundle**.
  `slow_params`/`slow_v_list` and `fast_params`/`fast_v_list` are parallel
  lists; per-axis all vectors must be equal length. The grid is
  `len(slow_v) × len(fast_v)`; at each grid point every slow param and every
  fast param is set together. Example — field-slow, (Vtg, Vbg)-line-fast:
  `s.multimegasweep([magnet.field], [B_vec], [k_tg.volt, k_bg.volt], [Vtgs, Vbgs], slow_delay=1, fast_delay=0.9)`.
- **`init_delay`** (2D only) — `True` applies `slow_delay` before the very
  first point; `False` skips it (the axis is already parked there).

All sweeps are SIGINT-interruptible: an interrupt finishes the current point,
sets `metadata['interrupted'] = True`, and marks the station interrupted (call
`reset()` or rebuild before the next sweep).

### `SweepResult` (dataclass)
`SweepResult(basedir, id, metadata, datapath)` — the run root, the integer run
id, the final `metadata` dict, and the on-disk `data.tsv.gz` path.

---

## Module-level helpers (`sweep.*`)

- `set_basedir(path)` — set the global `BASEDIR` used when a `Station` is built
  without an explicit `basedir`.
- `list_measurements(basedir=None)` — render a markdown table of runs in a
  basedir.
- `measurement_info(i, basedir=None)` — print one run's metadata.
- `set_shutdown_handler(fn)` / `request_shutdown()` — register a
  ramp-to-safe callback and trigger graceful shutdown (thread-safe; if a sweep
  is active it stops after the current point, then calls `fn`). Used by the UPS
  monitor.

---

## Data on disk (`sweep.db`)

Each run is a directory `<basedir>/<id>/` with `data.tsv(.gz)` (headerless TSV,
one row per point), `metadata.json`, and optional blobs (e.g. `plot.png`).

### `Writer(basedir, max_id=1_000_000, fsync_every=10)`
Creates the run directory at the lowest free integer id under `basedir`
(`.id`, `.dir`). `add_point(point)` / `add_points(points)` append rows
(fsynced every `fsync_every` points); `add_blob(name, bytes)` writes a sidecar
file (name may not be `data.tsv`/`data.tsv.gz`/`metadata.json`). `.metadata` is
a free dict saved to `metadata.json` on `close()`; on close the uncompressed
`data.tsv` is gzipped to `data.tsv.gz` (verified, then the plaintext removed).
Use as a context manager.

### `Reader(basedir, id)`
Reads a run back. `.metadata` (migrated to the current schema via
`migrate_metadata`), iteration yields rows of **strings** (no type conversion),
`all_data()` returns all rows, `blob(name)` reads a sidecar. `.datapath` is the
`data.tsv.gz` path. Use as a context manager. For numeric loads,
`np.loadtxt(reader.datapath, …)` or `hera.analysis.open_run`.

### Metadata keys written per sweep type
Common to all: `version`, `type` (`0D`/`1D`/`2D`), `function`, `columns`,
`comments`, `measurement_config`, `instruments`, `interrupted`, `start_time`,
`end_time`.

| function | additional keys |
|---|---|
| `sweep` | `param`, `setpoints`, `delay` |
| `multisweep` | `params`, `setpoints` (list of per-param vectors), `delay` |
| `megasweep` | `slow_param`, `fast_param`, `slow_setpoints`, `fast_setpoints`, `slow_delay`, `fast_delay` |
| `multimegasweep` | `slow_params`, `fast_params`, `slow_setpoints`, `fast_setpoints`, `slow_delay`, `fast_delay` |
| `watch` | `delay`, `max_duration` |

Two schemas coexist in older data — singular (`param`, `slow_param`) vs current
plural (`params`, `slow_params`). Read through `sweep.sweep_load` or
`hera.analysis.open_run`; don't hand-roll key access.

---

## Polygon rasters (`sweep.raster`)

Helpers for sweeping/plotting an arbitrary polygon region of a 2-D plane (e.g. a
bounded (Vtg, Vbg) window). A `multimegasweep` runs the rasterized point order;
these turn polygon vertices into that point list and back into a plot mesh.

### `rasterize(vertices, nx, ny, fast_axis, rev_x=False, rev_y=False)` → `(xs, ys)`
The x/y coordinates of the grid points **inside** the polygon. `vertices` is
`(N, 2)`; `nx`/`ny` are grid points per axis over the bounding box; `fast_axis`
is 0 if x is the inner (fast) axis, 1 if y; `rev_x`/`rev_y` reverse a sweep
direction. Returns two 1-D arrays in raster order — feed them as the co-swept
fast/slow vectors of a `multimegasweep`.

### `pcolorize_data(zs, vertices, nx, ny, fast_axis, rev_x=False, rev_y=False)` → `(xs_mat, ys_mat, zs_mat)`
Bin measured values `zs` (in rasterized point order) back onto the regular
bounding mesh for `plt.pcolormesh(xs_mat, ys_mat, zs_mat)`. Cells outside the
polygon are `NaN`. The `nx`/`ny`/`fast_axis`/`rev_*` arguments must match the
`rasterize` call that produced the sweep.

### `random_ngon_vertices(n)` → `(n, 2)` vertices
A random simple-ish n-gon, for tests/demos.

1	# `hera.analysis` API Reference
2	
3	Analysis primitives for `sweep` runs: open + summarize a run, resolve lock-in
4	channels and gains, re-form 2D fans into grids, compute gain-applied
5	resistances, and the Shubnikov–de Haas / gate-calibration math.
6	
7	Source: `src/hera/analysis.py`. Depends only on `numpy` + `scipy`.
8	
9	A *run* is a directory written by `sweep`: `data.tsv(.gz)` (headerless, one row
10	per setpoint) + `metadata.json` (column names, sweep config, comments).
11	
12	---
13	
14	## Loading runs
15	
16	### `open_run(path)` → `Run`
17	Open a run directory (e.g. `<notebook>/data/119`). Loads `metadata.json` and
18	`data.tsv(.gz)` into an `(rows, ncols)` float array; raises if the directory,
19	`metadata.json`, the `columns` entry, or the TSV is missing, or if the column
20	count disagrees with `metadata['columns']`.
21	
22	### `Run` (dataclass)
23	`Run(path, meta, cols, data)`.
24	
25	| member | description |
26	|---|---|
27	| `col(name)` | column `name` as a 1-D array; raises `KeyError` if absent, `ValueError` if the name is duplicated (use `col_at`) |
28	| `col_at(idx)` | column by index |
29	| `col_indices(name)` | all indices with column name `name` |
30	| `metadata` | alias for `meta` (the parsed `metadata.json` dict) |
31	| `recipe` | first metadata comment (conventional recipe slug), or `None` |
32	| `tags` | comments after the first |
33	| `swept_axis` | `metadata['param']` (1D sweeps) |
34	| `setpoints` | `metadata['setpoints']` as a list, or `None` |
35	| `interrupted` | `metadata['interrupted']` |
36	| `kind` | `metadata['type']` (`'0D'`/`'1D'`/`'2D'`) |
37	| `rows` | row count |
38	
39	Duplicate column names occur (planned setpoint + readback share a name; some
40	older data has two `T` columns). `col(name)` raises on duplicates — resolve
41	with `col_indices` + `col_at`.
42	
43	### `summarize_run(run)` → `str`
44	Multi-line human summary: recipe, type, sweep range + monotonicity, row
45	completeness vs planned setpoints, and mean/range T if a `T` column is present.
46	Lines with no data are omitted.
47	
48	---
49	
50	## Lock-in channel / gain model
51	
52	Shared with `hera.watch`. The physical value of a lock-in `*_X` column is
53	`X / gain`, with the gain read from `measurement_config` — never hardcode it.
54	
55	### `resolve_channels(meta, include=None)` → `list[Channel]`
56	Resolve every `_X` (in-phase) column into a `Channel`. Gains and role labels
57	come from `meta['measurement_config']`, matched `srN_X` ↔ `srN_gain` by the
58	channel's trailing integer (so both `sr0_X`↔`sr0_gain` and `sr830_1_X`↔`sr1_gain`
59	resolve); missing/zero gain defaults to `1.0`. `include` restricts to given
60	channel ids or column names. A channel `is_current` (reported as amps, not
61	converted to resistance) when its gain is negative, `|gain| ≥ 1e4`, or its
62	label mentions "current".
63	
64	### `Channel` (dataclass)
65	`col` (e.g. `'sr0_X'`), `idx` (column index), `cid` (id without `_X`), `n`
66	(trailing-integer index), `gain`, `label` (mc role string), `is_current`.
67	
68	### `current_channel(channels)` → `Channel | None`
69	The single transimpedance current channel, or `None` if not exactly one. This
70	is the denominator of four-probe resistance R = V / I.
71	
72	---
73	
74	## Fan re-forming and resistances
75	
76	### `fan_grids(run, columns=None)` → `FanGrids`
77	Re-form a 2D fan (a flat-row `megasweep`/`multimegasweep`) into per-column
78	grids, keeping only complete slow rows. `run` is a directory, path, or loaded
79	`Run`. `nfast` (points per slow row) comes from `metadata['fast_setpoints']`
80	— never hardcoded; trailing partial rows of an in-progress sweep are dropped
81	(`nrows = total // nfast`). `columns` restricts which columns are retained.
82	
83	### `FanGrids` (dataclass)
84	`nrows`, `nfast`, `cols`, `data` (truncated to whole rows), `meta`,
85	`slow_param`.
86	- `grid(name)` → `(nrows, nfast)` array (duplicate names resolve to the first
87	  occurrence, i.e. the planned setpoint).
88	- `slow` → slow-axis value per row, `(nrows,)`.
89	- `metadata` → alias for `meta`.
90	
91	### `resistance_grids(fan, channels=None)` → `ResistanceGrids`
92	Per-channel four-probe resistance grids `R = (V / gain_V) / I` from a
93	`FanGrids`, where `I` is the **measured** drain current
94	`I = X_cur / gain_cur` (a grid — it sags where the device is resistive), not a
95	nominal bias. Gains come from `measurement_config`. Raises if not exactly one
96	current channel is resolvable. `channels` restricts the voltage channels
97	returned. Returned R is **signed** (X/I): take `np.abs` for Rxx, keep the sign
98	for Rxy/Hall.
99	
100	### `ResistanceGrids` (dataclass)
101	`current` (I grid, A), `current_channel` (cid), `R` (dict: voltage cid →
102	signed R grid, Ω).
103	
104	---
105	
106	## Shubnikov–de Haas
107	
108	### `field_invB(B_start, B_end, N)` → `np.ndarray`
109	`N` field points from `B_start` to `B_end`, **uniform in 1/B** (SdH
110	oscillations are periodic in 1/B). Both endpoints must be `> 0`. Argument order
111	sets sweep direction. Sweeping these setpoints hands `sdh_fft` an already-even
112	1/B record (no resample needed).
113	
114	### `sdh_fft(R_grid, B, *, b_range=None, nfft=512, bg_degree=5, window='hann', log=True, floor=1.0, uniform_rtol=0.1)` → `(freqs, spec)`
115	Per-column SdH FFT in 1/B.
116	
117	- **Input `R_grid` is `(n_B, n_fast)`** — rows are field (the `FanGrids` row
118	  axis), columns are the fast axis. **2-D is required**; a single trace must be
119	  passed as `R[:, None]` (and the output column squeezed back). Raises if
120	  `R_grid.shape[0] != len(B)`.
121	- `B` is the per-row field `(n_B,)`, arbitrarily spaced.
122	- Per column: select `b_range`, optionally `log10(max(R, floor))`, subtract a
123	  degree-`bg_degree` polynomial background **in B-space** (`None` skips — the
124	  magnetoresistance background is smooth in B, not 1/B, so it is removed before
125	  the 1/B step), then FFT in 1/B. The 1/B resample is conditional: data already
126	  uniform in 1/B (decided from the spacing distribution within `uniform_rtol`)
127	  is FFT'd directly, zero-padded to `nfft`; uniform-in-B data is interpolated
128	  onto a regular `nfft`-point 1/B grid.
129	- **Returns `(freqs, spec)`**: `freqs` in Tesla `(n_freq,)`, `spec` the FFT
130	  magnitude **`(n_fast, n_freq)`** (note the transpose vs the input).
131	
132	### `sdh_onset(R, B, *, b_hi=None, b_lo=0.3, r_full_scale=None, headroom=0.95, bg_degree=5, f_min=3.0, snr_threshold=5.0, n_periods=3.0, min_periods=2.0, step_frac=0.25, gap_widths=0.5, min_pts=8, max_tones=8, tone_floor_mult=4.0, marginal_mult=2.0)` → `SdhOnset`
133	Per-tone low-B onsets of the SdH oscillations in a single trace.
134	**`R` is a single 1-D longitudinal-resistance trace `(n_B,)`** (contrast
135	`sdh_fft`'s 2-D grid); `B` is the matching field `(n_B,)`. Removes a B-space
136	polynomial background, identifies every SdH tone via nested high-B FFT scans,
137	then walks each tone's Gaussian matched filter (FWHM = `n_periods` periods of
138	that tone) from high B down to where its amplitude sinks into the record's
139	white-noise floor — a statistical (≈`snr_threshold`·σ) onset, which can
140	legitimately sit below a by-eye read. `onset_b` is the minimum onset over
141	robust tones — the `landau-fan` step-1 `B_lo`, correct even when a light tone
142	outlives the dominant one. Pass `r_full_scale` (sensitivity / I_bias, Ω) to
143	enable soft-clip detection: samples ≥ `headroom`× full scale truncate the
144	analysis window (reported via `clip_high_b`) with a warning.
145	**Failure is never a nan** — raises `SdhOnsetError` (a `ValueError`: record
146	too short, no tones above the spectral floor, or no tone trackable) with

# `hera.analysis` API Reference

Analysis primitives for `sweep` runs: open + summarize a run, resolve lock-in
channels and gains, re-form 2D fans into grids, compute gain-applied
resistances, and the Shubnikov–de Haas / gate-calibration math.

Source: `src/hera/analysis.py`. Depends only on `numpy` + `scipy`.

A *run* is a directory written by `sweep`: `data.tsv(.gz)` (headerless, one row
per setpoint) + `metadata.json` (column names, sweep config, comments).

---

## Loading runs

### `open_run(path)` → `Run`
Open a run directory (e.g. `<notebook>/data/119`). Loads `metadata.json` and
`data.tsv(.gz)` into an `(rows, ncols)` float array; raises if the directory,
`metadata.json`, the `columns` entry, or the TSV is missing, or if the column
count disagrees with `metadata['columns']`.

### `Run` (dataclass)
`Run(path, meta, cols, data)`.

| member | description |
|---|---|
| `col(name)` | column `name` as a 1-D array; raises `KeyError` if absent, `ValueError` if the name is duplicated (use `col_at`) |
| `col_at(idx)` | column by index |
| `col_indices(name)` | all indices with column name `name` |
| `metadata` | alias for `meta` (the parsed `metadata.json` dict) |
| `recipe` | first metadata comment (conventional recipe slug), or `None` |
| `tags` | comments after the first |
| `swept_axis` | `metadata['param']` (1D sweeps) |
| `setpoints` | `metadata['setpoints']` as a list, or `None` |
| `interrupted` | `metadata['interrupted']` |
| `kind` | `metadata['type']` (`'0D'`/`'1D'`/`'2D'`) |
| `rows` | row count |

Duplicate column names occur (planned setpoint + readback share a name; some
older data has two `T` columns). `col(name)` raises on duplicates — resolve
with `col_indices` + `col_at`.

### `summarize_run(run)` → `str`
Multi-line human summary: recipe, type, sweep range + monotonicity, row
completeness vs planned setpoints, and mean/range T if a `T` column is present.
Lines with no data are omitted.

---

## Lock-in channel / gain model

Shared with `hera.watch`. The physical value of a lock-in `*_X` column is
`X / gain`, with the gain read from `measurement_config` — never hardcode it.

### `resolve_channels(meta, include=None)` → `list[Channel]`
Resolve every `_X` (in-phase) column into a `Channel`. Gains and role labels
come from `meta['measurement_config']`, matched `srN_X` ↔ `srN_gain` by the
channel's trailing integer (so both `sr0_X`↔`sr0_gain` and `sr830_1_X`↔`sr1_gain`
resolve); missing/zero gain defaults to `1.0`. `include` restricts to given
channel ids or column names. A channel `is_current` (reported as amps, not
converted to resistance) when its gain is negative, `|gain| ≥ 1e4`, or its
label mentions "current".

### `Channel` (dataclass)
`col` (e.g. `'sr0_X'`), `idx` (column index), `cid` (id without `_X`), `n`
(trailing-integer index), `gain`, `label` (mc role string), `is_current`.

### `current_channel(channels)` → `Channel | None`
The single transimpedance current channel, or `None` if not exactly one. This
is the denominator of four-probe resistance R = V / I.

---

## Fan re-forming and resistances

### `fan_grids(run, columns=None)` → `FanGrids`
Re-form a 2D fan (a flat-row `megasweep`/`multimegasweep`) into per-column
grids, keeping only complete slow rows. `run` is a directory, path, or loaded
`Run`. `nfast` (points per slow row) comes from `metadata['fast_setpoints']`
— never hardcoded; trailing partial rows of an in-progress sweep are dropped
(`nrows = total // nfast`). `columns` restricts which columns are retained.

### `FanGrids` (dataclass)
`nrows`, `nfast`, `cols`, `data` (truncated to whole rows), `meta`,
`slow_param`.
- `grid(name)` → `(nrows, nfast)` array (duplicate names resolve to the first
  occurrence, i.e. the planned setpoint).
- `slow` → slow-axis value per row, `(nrows,)`.
- `metadata` → alias for `meta`.

### `resistance_grids(fan, channels=None)` → `ResistanceGrids`
Per-channel four-probe resistance grids `R = (V / gain_V) / I` from a
`FanGrids`, where `I` is the **measured** drain current
`I = X_cur / gain_cur` (a grid — it sags where the device is resistive), not a
nominal bias. Gains come from `measurement_config`. Raises if not exactly one
current channel is resolvable. `channels` restricts the voltage channels
returned. Returned R is **signed** (X/I): take `np.abs` for Rxx, keep the sign
for Rxy/Hall.

### `ResistanceGrids` (dataclass)
`current` (I grid, A), `current_channel` (cid), `R` (dict: voltage cid →
signed R grid, Ω).

---

## Shubnikov–de Haas

### `field_invB(B_start, B_end, N)` → `np.ndarray`
`N` field points from `B_start` to `B_end`, **uniform in 1/B** (SdH
oscillations are periodic in 1/B). Both endpoints must be `> 0`. Argument order
sets sweep direction. Sweeping these setpoints hands `sdh_fft` an already-even
1/B record (no resample needed).

### `sdh_fft(R_grid, B, *, b_range=None, nfft=512, bg_degree=5, window='hann', log=True, floor=1.0, uniform_rtol=0.1)` → `(freqs, spec)`
Per-column SdH FFT in 1/B.

- **Input `R_grid` is `(n_B, n_fast)`** — rows are field (the `FanGrids` row
  axis), columns are the fast axis. **2-D is required**; a single trace must be
  passed as `R[:, None]` (and the output column squeezed back). Raises if
  `R_grid.shape[0] != len(B)`.
- `B` is the per-row field `(n_B,)`, arbitrarily spaced.
- Per column: select `b_range`, optionally `log10(max(R, floor))`, subtract a
  degree-`bg_degree` polynomial background **in B-space** (`None` skips — the
  magnetoresistance background is smooth in B, not 1/B, so it is removed before
  the 1/B step), then FFT in 1/B. The 1/B resample is conditional: data already
  uniform in 1/B (decided from the spacing distribution within `uniform_rtol`)
  is FFT'd directly, zero-padded to `nfft`; uniform-in-B data is interpolated
  onto a regular `nfft`-point 1/B grid.
- **Returns `(freqs, spec)`**: `freqs` in Tesla `(n_freq,)`, `spec` the FFT
  magnitude **`(n_fast, n_freq)`** (note the transpose vs the input).

### `sdh_onset(R, B, *, b_hi=None, b_lo=0.3, r_full_scale=None, headroom=0.95, bg_degree=5, f_min=3.0, snr_threshold=5.0, n_periods=3.0, min_periods=2.0, step_frac=0.25, gap_widths=0.5, min_pts=8, max_tones=8, tone_floor_mult=4.0, marginal_mult=2.0)` → `SdhOnset`
Per-tone low-B onsets of the SdH oscillations in a single trace.
**`R` is a single 1-D longitudinal-resistance trace `(n_B,)`** (contrast
`sdh_fft`'s 2-D grid); `B` is the matching field `(n_B,)`. Removes a B-space
polynomial background, identifies every SdH tone via nested high-B FFT scans,
then walks each tone's Gaussian matched filter (FWHM = `n_periods` periods of
that tone) from high B down to where its amplitude sinks into the record's
white-noise floor — a statistical (≈`snr_threshold`·σ) onset, which can
legitimately sit below a by-eye read. `onset_b` is the minimum onset over
robust tones — the `landau-fan` step-1 `B_lo`, correct even when a light tone
outlives the dominant one. Pass `r_full_scale` (sensitivity / I_bias, Ω) to
enable soft-clip detection: samples ≥ `headroom`× full scale truncate the
analysis window (reported via `clip_high_b`) with a warning.
**Failure is never a nan** — raises `SdhOnsetError` (a `ValueError`: record
too short, no tones above the spectral floor, or no tone trackable) with
specifics; partial failures warn and land in `.untracked`.

### `SdhOnset` (dataclass)
`onset_b` (min onset over robust tones, Tesla — the record's low edge, flagged,
when the carrying tone is *censored*, i.e. still above threshold at the last
window), `onset_freq` (tone carrying it), `clip_high_b` / `b_lo_record` (the
analyzed window's edges), `noise_sigma`, `tones` (list of `SdhTone`, contrast
descending), `untracked` (`(freq, reason)` pairs). Convenience properties map
to the dominant tone: `consensus_freq`, `b_centers`, `snr` (the old
`peak_freq` field is gone). `summary()` renders the whole read — headline,
per-tone table with flags, untracked reasons — for a notebook cell.

### `SdhTone` (dataclass)
One tone's track: `freq`, `contrast`, `onset_b`, flags `censored` /
`revived` (above-threshold windows exist below the gap-walk stop) /
`marginal` (peak SNR < `marginal_mult`×threshold; excluded from the headline) /
`near_residual` (filter passband overlaps the detrend-residual band; excluded
from the headline unless a tracked harmonic corroborates it), `n_periods` /
`win_invB` (actual filter geometry), `harmonic_of` (freq of the stronger tone
this sits at ~k× of, else `None`), curves `b_centers` / `snr` / `amp`, and
`delta_f(b_max)` — the per-tone FFT resolution `1/(1/onset_b − 1/b_max)`.

---

## Gate calibration

> **Units — SI.** `GateCalibration` and `luttinger_frequency` work entirely in
> SI: density **n in m⁻²**, displacement field **D in V/m**, frequency in
> Tesla. (For the conventional ×10¹² cm⁻² display unit, scale n by `1e-16`.)
> The separate `sharpelab_nb.gates` conversion helpers (`calc_nD`,
> `calc_gate_voltages`, …) use **n in 10¹² cm⁻²** — do not feed an SI density
> from here into those, or vice versa.

### `GateCalibration` (frozen dataclass)
`GateCalibration(c_tg, c_bg, n_offset=0.0, D_offset=0.0)` — areal capacitances
(F/m²), `n_offset` (m⁻²), `D_offset` (V/m). Construct once per session, then:

```
n = (c_tg·V_tg + c_bg·V_bg) / e   + n_offset      [m⁻²]
D = (c_tg·V_tg − c_bg·V_bg) / (2·ε₀) + D_offset   [V/m]
```

- `density(V_tg, V_bg)` → n `(m⁻²)`.
- `displacement_field(V_tg, V_bg)` → D `(V/m)`.
- `n_D(V_tg, V_bg)` → `(n, D)`.
- `from_thicknesses(t_tg, t_bg, t_bgSiO2=0.0, *, n_offset=0.0, D_offset=0.0, kappa_hBN=3.0, kappa_SiO2=3.9)` — build from gate-stack geometry (metres) instead of areal capacitances; `t_bgSiO2=0` for a metal/graphite back gate.

All accept scalars or arrays. Physical constants come from `scipy.constants`.

### `luttinger_frequency(n)` → `np.ndarray`
Full-density Onsager (SdH) frequency `F = |n|·h / (4·e)`, in Tesla, for a
single Fermi surface carrying the full density. **`n` is in SI m⁻²** — feed
`GateCalibration.density` output directly. The 4 is the spin×valley Landau
degeneracy; returns the `|n|` form (positive for either carrier sign).

import time

import numpy as np


def autorange_sr830s(
    sr830_current: object,
    sr830s: list[object],
    lower_lim: float = 1e-6,
) -> None:
    """Auto-adjust SR830 sensitivity based on current reading vs. range.

    Checks the phase of the current-measuring SR830 to verify valid
    measurement conditions, then iterates through the other lock-ins
    and adjusts sensitivity up or down as needed.

    Waits 10x the time constant between sensitivity changes per the
    SR830 manual guidelines.

    Args:
        sr830_current: The SR830 instrument measuring current. Used for
            phase check only.
        sr830s: List of SR830 instruments to auto-range.
        lower_lim: Minimum sensitivity threshold. Won't decrement below this.
    """
    if len(sr830s) == 0:
        return

    p = sr830_current.P()  # type: ignore[union-attr]
    if np.abs(p) < 160:
        return

    for s in sr830s:

        def autorange_once(sr830: object) -> bool:
            r = sr830.R()  # type: ignore[union-attr]
            sens = sr830.sensitivity()  # type: ignore[union-attr]

            if r > 0.9 * sens:
                return sr830.increment_sensitivity()  # type: ignore[union-attr]
            elif r < 0.1 * sens:
                if sens <= lower_lim:
                    return False
                else:
                    return sr830.decrement_sensitivity()  # type: ignore[union-attr]
            return False

        adjustments = 0
        while autorange_once(s) and adjustments < 3:
            adjustments += 1
            time.sleep(10 * s.time_constant())  # type: ignore[union-attr]

8	_EPS0 = 8.8541878128e-12  # F/m (CODATA 2018)
9	_E = 1.602176634e-19  # C (exact)
10	
11	
12	def stack_capacitance(layers: Sequence[tuple[float, float]]) -> float:
13	    """Areal capacitance (F/m^2) of a series dielectric stack.
14	
15	    Args:
16	        layers: ``(thickness_nm, kappa)`` per layer, in series — e.g.
17	            ``[(12, 3)]`` for 12 nm of hBN, or ``[(12, 3), (285, 3.9)]``
18	            for hBN backed by SiO2. Zero-thickness layers contribute
19	            nothing.
20	
21	    Returns:
22	        Capacitance per unit area (F/m^2).
23	    """
24	    total = 0.0
25	    for t_nm, kappa in layers:
26	        total += (t_nm * 1e-9) / kappa
27	    return _EPS0 / total
28	
29	
30	def calc_nD(
31	    Vtg: Any,
32	    Vbg: Any,
33	    c_tg: float,
34	    c_bg: float,
35	    n_offset: float = 0.0,
36	    D_offset: float = 0.0,
37	) -> tuple[Any, Any]:
38	    """Convert gate voltages to carrier density and displacement field.
39	
40	    Canonical (n, D) conversion, parametrized by areal gate capacitances
41	    (:func:`stack_capacitance`) — the quantity calibration actually
42	    refines: a fitted CNP-line slope dVtg/dVbg is ``-c_bg/c_tg``, and a
43	    quantum-Hall lever-arm check sets the absolute scale.
44	
45	    Args:
46	        Vtg: Top gate voltage (V).
47	        Vbg: Back gate voltage (V).
48	        c_tg: Top gate areal capacitance (F/m^2).
49	        c_bg: Back gate areal capacitance (F/m^2).
50	        n_offset: Density offset (10^12 cm^-2).
51	        D_offset: Displacement field offset (V/nm).
52	
53	    Returns:
54	        (n, D): n in 10^12 cm^-2, D in V/nm.
55	    """
56	    n = (c_tg * Vtg + c_bg * Vbg) / _E * 1e-16 + n_offset
57	    D = 0.5 * (c_tg * Vtg - c_bg * Vbg) / _EPS0 * 1e-9 + D_offset
58	    return n, D

62	    n: Any,

66	    n_offset: float = 0.0,
67	    D_offset: float = 0.0,
68	) -> tuple[Any, Any]:
69	    """Convert (n, D) to gate voltages — inverse of :func:`calc_nD`.
70	
71	    Args:
72	        n: Carrier density (10^12 cm^-2).

from collections.abc import Sequence
from typing import Any

import numpy as np
import numpy.typing as npt
from sweep import raster

_EPS0 = 8.8541878128e-12  # F/m (CODATA 2018)
_E = 1.602176634e-19  # C (exact)


def stack_capacitance(layers: Sequence[tuple[float, float]]) -> float:
    """Areal capacitance (F/m^2) of a series dielectric stack.

    Args:
        layers: ``(thickness_nm, kappa)`` per layer, in series — e.g.
            ``[(12, 3)]`` for 12 nm of hBN, or ``[(12, 3), (285, 3.9)]``
            for hBN backed by SiO2. Zero-thickness layers contribute
            nothing.

    Returns:
        Capacitance per unit area (F/m^2).
    """
    total = 0.0
    for t_nm, kappa in layers:
        total += (t_nm * 1e-9) / kappa
    return _EPS0 / total


def calc_nD(
    Vtg: Any,
    Vbg: Any,
    c_tg: float,
    c_bg: float,
    n_offset: float = 0.0,
    D_offset: float = 0.0,
) -> tuple[Any, Any]:
    """Convert gate voltages to carrier density and displacement field.

    Canonical (n, D) conversion, parametrized by areal gate capacitances
    (:func:`stack_capacitance`) — the quantity calibration actually
    refines: a fitted CNP-line slope dVtg/dVbg is ``-c_bg/c_tg``, and a
    quantum-Hall lever-arm check sets the absolute scale.

    Args:
        Vtg: Top gate voltage (V).
        Vbg: Back gate voltage (V).
        c_tg: Top gate areal capacitance (F/m^2).
        c_bg: Back gate areal capacitance (F/m^2).
        n_offset: Density offset (10^12 cm^-2).
        D_offset: Displacement field offset (V/nm).

    Returns:
        (n, D): n in 10^12 cm^-2, D in V/nm.
    """
    n = (c_tg * Vtg + c_bg * Vbg) / _E * 1e-16 + n_offset
    D = 0.5 * (c_tg * Vtg - c_bg * Vbg) / _EPS0 * 1e-9 + D_offset
    return n, D


def calc_gate_voltages(
    n: Any,
    D: Any,
    c_tg: float,
    c_bg: float,
    n_offset: float = 0.0,
    D_offset: float = 0.0,
) -> tuple[Any, Any]:
    """Convert (n, D) to gate voltages — inverse of :func:`calc_nD`.

    Args:
        n: Carrier density (10^12 cm^-2).
        D: Displacement field (V/nm).
        c_tg: Top gate areal capacitance (F/m^2).
        c_bg: Back gate areal capacitance (F/m^2).
        n_offset: Density offset (10^12 cm^-2).
        D_offset: Displacement field offset (V/nm).

    Returns:
        (Vtg, Vbg) gate voltages (V). Scalar args return Python floats
        (so ``float(Vtg)`` is unnecessary); array args return arrays.
    """
    n = np.asarray(n, dtype=float)
    D = np.asarray(D, dtype=float)
    n_si = (n - n_offset) * 1e16  # m^-2
    D_si = (D - D_offset) * 1e9  # V/m
    Vtg = (0.5 * _E * n_si + _EPS0 * D_si) / c_tg
    Vbg = (0.5 * _E * n_si - _EPS0 * D_si) / c_bg
    if Vtg.ndim == 0:
        return float(Vtg), float(Vbg)
    return Vtg, Vbg


def calculate_gate_voltages(
    n: Any,
    D: Any,
    dtg: float = 16,
    dbg: float = 25.5,
    ep: float = 3,
) -> tuple[Any, Any]:
    """Convert carrier density and displacement field to gate voltages.

    Single-dielectric special case of :func:`calc_gate_voltages` (both
    gates pure hBN, no offsets), parametrized by thickness. Prefer the
    capacitance form for new work.

    Args:
        n: Carrier density (10^12 cm^-2).
        D: Displacement field (V/nm).
        dtg: Top gate dielectric thickness (nm).
        dbg: Back gate dielectric thickness (nm).
        ep: Dielectric constant of hBN.

    Returns:
        (Vtg, Vbg) gate voltages.
    """
    return calc_gate_voltages(
        n, D, stack_capacitance([(dtg, ep)]), stack_capacitance([(dbg, ep)])
    )

23	2. calibrate a baseline line ``b0`` + noise ``sigma_I`` from the first safe stretch of
24	   the push (``|V| <= base_V``),
25	3. run a CUSUM on the local slope-excess z-score — how far the local ``dI/dV`` sits
26	   above ``b0``, in units of the local slope noise — resetting on dips.
27

29	several; transient noise never accumulates. No tail-confirmation: live, a false abort
30	is cheap (restart the sweep) and a missed leak is expensive (dead device), so it
31	commits forward. It assumes **one continuous push from parked-safe** — a chunked
32	sweep's per-segment DC offset steps fake a sloped baseline and false-trip it.
33	
34	The default ``(slack, H)`` and the inset applied to the reported onset are
35	**heuristics** (n=1 device, QC0426 replay); tune them against a live continuous push.
36	See ``hera/recipes/device-init/gate-leakage-survey.md``.
37	"""
38	from contextlib import contextmanager
39	from typing import Any, Callable, Iterator, Protocol
40	
41	import numpy as np
42	
43	_K = 1.4826  # MAD -> sigma for normal noise
44	
45	
46	class _Interruptible(Protocol):
47	    interrupt_requested: bool
48

50	class LeakageDetector:
51	    """Causal, self-calibrating dI/dV CUSUM leakage detector for a continuous push.
52	
53	    Feed it ``(V, I)`` per sweep point via :meth:`update`. After it has calibrated a
54	    baseline from the first safe stretch (``|V| <= base_V``), each point updates a CUSUM
55	    on the local slope-excess z-score; ``update`` returns ``True`` once the CUSUM crosses
56	    ``H`` (the trip), and :attr:`trip_V` holds the foot voltage where the accumulation
57	    began.
58	
59	    Args:
60	        base_V: Calibrate the baseline from points within this ``|V|`` of 0 (the safe
61	            start of the push).
62	        min_base: Minimum baseline points before calibrating.
63	        skip: Drop this many leading points (settling) from the baseline fit.
64	        win_V: Trailing-window half-width (volts) for the local ``dI/dV`` fit.
65	        sm_win: Causal median-filter window (points).
66	        slack: CUSUM slack in slope-sigmas — drift below this does not accumulate.
67	        H: CUSUM alarm bound; the gate trips when the accumulator exceeds it.
68	    """
69	
70	    def __init__(
71	        self,
72	        base_V: float = 2.5,
73	        min_base: int = 10,
74	        skip: int = 3,
75	        win_V: float = 0.4,
76	        sm_win: int = 5,
77	        slack: float = 4.0,
78	        H: float = 12.0,
79	    ) -> None:
80	        self.base_V, self.min_base, self.skip = base_V, min_base, skip
81	        self.win_V, self.sm_win = win_V, sm_win
82	        self.slack, self.H = slack, H
83	        self.V: list[float] = []
84	        self.Iraw: list[float] = []
85	        self.Ism: list[float] = []
86	        self.b0: float | None = None
87	        self.sigma_I: float | None = None
88	        self.S = 0.0
89	        self.last_z = 0.0
90	        self.run_start: float | None = None
91	        self.tripped = False
92	        self.trip_V: float | None = None
93	
94	    def update(self, V: float, I: float) -> bool:
95	        """Feed one sweep point. Returns ``True`` once tripped (=> request interrupt)."""
96	        if self.tripped:
97	            return True
98	        self.V.append(V)
99	        self.Iraw.append(I)
100	        # causal median filter: rejects spikes and smooths in one step
101	        n = len(self.Iraw)
102	        self.Ism.append(float(np.median(self.Iraw[max(0, n - self.sm_win):n])))
103	        Va = np.array(self.V)
104	        Ia = np.array(self.Ism)
105	
106	        # calibrate baseline once we've pushed past base_V with enough safe points
107	        if self.b0 is None:
108	            base = np.abs(Va) <= self.base_V
109	            if abs(V) > self.base_V and base.sum() >= self.min_base:
110	                Vb, Ib = Va[base][self.skip:], Ia[base][self.skip:]
111	                self.b0, a = np.polyfit(Vb, Ib, 1)
112	                resid = Ib - (a + self.b0 * Vb)
113	                self.sigma_I = max(_K * np.median(np.abs(resid - np.median(resid))), 1e-13)
114	            return False
115	        assert self.sigma_I is not None
116	
117	        # local slope over the trailing win_V window (buffer is all past/outward pts)
118	        sel = np.abs(Va - V) <= self.win_V
119	        Vw, Iw = Va[sel], Ia[sel]
120	        if len(Vw) < 4 or np.ptp(Vw) == 0:
121	            return False
122	        cf = np.polyfit(Vw, Iw, 1)
123	        resid = Iw - np.polyval(cf, Vw)
124	        # LOCAL noise, floored by baseline noise: a noisy stretch inflates this so z
125	        # shrinks (no false trip); a clean rising stretch keeps z high.
126	        sigma_loc = max(_K * np.median(np.abs(resid - np.median(resid))), self.sigma_I)
127	        se = sigma_loc / np.sqrt(np.sum((Vw - Vw.mean()) ** 2))
128	        self.last_z = (cf[0] - self.b0) / se  # slope-excess in sigmas (leak => +)
129

133	        if self.S > self.H:

136	            return True
137	        return False

304	        if avg_n is not None:
305	            k.write(f"SENS:AVER:COUNT {saved_count}")

        base_V: float = 2.5,
        min_base: int = 10,
        skip: int = 3,
        win_V: float = 0.4,
        sm_win: int = 5,
        slack: float = 4.0,
        H: float = 12.0,
    ) -> None:
        self.base_V, self.min_base, self.skip = base_V, min_base, skip
        self.win_V, self.sm_win = win_V, sm_win
        self.slack, self.H = slack, H
        self.V: list[float] = []
        self.Iraw: list[float] = []
        self.Ism: list[float] = []
        self.b0: float | None = None
        self.sigma_I: float | None = None
        self.S = 0.0
        self.last_z = 0.0
        self.run_start: float | None = None
        self.tripped = False
        self.trip_V: float | None = None

    def update(self, V: float, I: float) -> bool:
        """Feed one sweep point. Returns ``True`` once tripped (=> request interrupt)."""
        if self.tripped:
            return True
        self.V.append(V)
        self.Iraw.append(I)
        # causal median filter: rejects spikes and smooths in one step
        n = len(self.Iraw)
        self.Ism.append(float(np.median(self.Iraw[max(0, n - self.sm_win):n])))
        Va = np.array(self.V)
        Ia = np.array(self.Ism)

        # calibrate baseline once we've pushed past base_V with enough safe points
        if self.b0 is None:
            base = np.abs(Va) <= self.base_V
            if abs(V) > self.base_V and base.sum() >= self.min_base:
                Vb, Ib = Va[base][self.skip:], Ia[base][self.skip:]
                self.b0, a = np.polyfit(Vb, Ib, 1)
                resid = Ib - (a + self.b0 * Vb)
                self.sigma_I = max(_K * np.median(np.abs(resid - np.median(resid))), 1e-13)
            return False
        assert self.sigma_I is not None

        # local slope over the trailing win_V window (buffer is all past/outward pts)
        sel = np.abs(Va - V) <= self.win_V
        Vw, Iw = Va[sel], Ia[sel]
        if len(Vw) < 4 or np.ptp(Vw) == 0:
            return False
        cf = np.polyfit(Vw, Iw, 1)
        resid = Iw - np.polyval(cf, Vw)
        # LOCAL noise, floored by baseline noise: a noisy stretch inflates this so z
        # shrinks (no false trip); a clean rising stretch keeps z high.
        sigma_loc = max(_K * np.median(np.abs(resid - np.median(resid))), self.sigma_I)
        se = sigma_loc / np.sqrt(np.sum((Vw - Vw.mean()) ** 2))
        self.last_z = (cf[0] - self.b0) / se  # slope-excess in sigmas (leak => +)

        if self.S <= 0:
            self.run_start = V
        self.S = max(0.0, self.S + self.last_z - self.slack)
        if self.S > self.H:
            self.tripped = True
            self.trip_V = self.run_start  # foot = where accumulation began
            return True
        return False


def leakage_check(
    detector: LeakageDetector,
    curr_param: Callable[[], float],
    volt_param: Callable[[], float],
    station: _Interruptible,
) -> None:
    """Low-level ``register_run_before`` adapter — re-reads the SMU each point.

    ``station`` is injected from the run-before context, so register with the *other*
    args only; passing ``station`` in ``args`` too double-binds it
    (``TypeError: got multiple values for argument 'station'``). For a Keithley 2400,
    prefer :func:`k2400_leakage_guard`, which wires this up and configures the
    instrument for you. Use this directly only for a non-2400 source::

        s.register_run_before(leakage_check, args=(detector, gate.curr, gate.volt))

    For zero extra instrument reads, prefer :func:`leakage_check_after`.
    """
    if detector.update(volt_param(), curr_param()):
        station.interrupt_requested = True


def leakage_check_after(
    detector: LeakageDetector,
    station: _Interruptible,
    data: list[float],
    *,
    i_col: int = 2,
    v_col: int = 1,
) -> None:
    """Low-level ``register_run_after`` adapter — **zero** extra instrument reads.

    Instead of re-reading the SMU, it feeds the detector what the sweep already
    measured. The run-after ``data`` row is ``[time, setpoint, *followed_params]``, so
    ``v_col=1`` is the commanded gate voltage and ``i_col`` is the gate-current
    followed-param column. ``station``/``data`` are injected from the run-after
    context, so register with the detector only::

        s.register_run_after(leakage_check_after, args=(detector,))      # i_col=2
        # gate current is not the first followed param -> pin its column:
        s.register_run_after(partial(leakage_check_after, i_col=N), args=(detector,))

    Correctness conditions (not optional notes):

    - The **gate current must be a followed param**; ``i_col = 2 + its fp position``
      (2 if it is the first/only followed param).
    - ``data[i_col]`` is **gain-divided** (the station stores ``p() / gain``) — follow
      the gate-current param with ``gain=1`` so the detector sees the true current.
    - **V = setpoint** is exact and noise-free; for a voltage source it equals
      ``volt()``.
    - This aborts **one point past** the foot (vs ``run_before``'s one-before) — a
      single-point overshoot, acceptable under "false abort cheap, missed leak
      expensive".
    - Net vs the re-reading guard: **3 reads/pt -> 1 (~3x faster), identical detection.**
    """
    if detector.update(float(data[v_col]), float(data[i_col])):
        station.interrupt_requested = True


class _K2400Guard:
    """The bound guard yielded by :func:`k2400_leakage_guard`."""

    def __init__(self, detector: LeakageDetector, k: Any) -> None:
        self._detector = detector
        self._k = k

    def check(self, station: _Interruptible) -> None:
        """Register as ``s.register_run_before(guard.check, args=())`` — ``station``
        comes from the run-before context, so do *not* also pass it in ``args``.

        Re-reads the SMU each point (``volt()`` + ``curr()``); for zero extra reads use
        :meth:`check_after`.
        """
        if self._detector.update(float(self._k.volt()), float(self._k.curr())):
            station.interrupt_requested = True

    def check_after(
        self,
        station: _Interruptible,
        data: list[float],
        *,
        i_col: int = 2,
        v_col: int = 1,
    ) -> None:
        """``register_run_after`` form — **zero** extra instrument reads.

        Feeds the detector ``V = setpoint`` (``data[v_col]``) and ``I`` = the measured
        gate-current followed-param (``data[i_col]``, which must be followed with
        ``gain=1`` so it is the true current). Register with ``args=()``; pin a
        non-default current column via :func:`functools.partial`::

            s.register_run_after(guard.check_after, args=())                    # i_col=2
            s.register_run_after(partial(guard.check_after, i_col=N), args=())  # else

        See :func:`leakage_check_after` for the full correctness conditions.
        """
        if self._detector.update(float(data[v_col]), float(data[i_col])):
            station.interrupt_requested = True

    @property
    def detector(self) -> LeakageDetector:
        return self._detector

    @property
    def tripped(self) -> bool:
        return self._detector.tripped

    @property
    def trip_V(self) -> float | None:
        return self._detector.trip_V


@contextmanager
def k2400_leakage_guard(
    k: Any,
    *,
    nplc: int = 10,
    avg_n: int | None = 6,
    rangei: float | None = 1e-9,
    slack: float = 4.0,
    H: float = 12.0,
) -> Iterator[_K2400Guard]:
    """Configure a Keithley 2400 for a leakage survey, yield a guard, restore on exit.

    The survey is always run on a 2400, so this bakes in the good setup (pA current
    range, high integration, repeat-averaging) and pulls ``curr``/``volt`` off the
    instrument — the caller can't wire the wrong channel or forget to restore::

        with k2400_leakage_guard(k_bg) as guard:
            s.register_run_after(guard.check_after, args=())   # zero extra reads
            try:
                s.sweep(k_bg.volt, ramp, delay=delay)
            finally:
                s.ramp(k_bg.volt, 0)
        print(guard.trip_V)            # k_bg restored here

    Args:
        k: A qcodes Keithley 2400 instrument.
        nplc: Current-channel integration (``nplci``); 10 is the 2400 max.
        avg_n: Repeat-average filter count (1-100), or ``None`` to leave the filter
            untouched. The 2400 averaging filter has no qcodes parameter, so this is
            set via raw SCPI. **[BETA] verify the SCPI on the instrument.**
        rangei: Current range to force (pA-resolution default), or ``None`` to leave it.
        slack, H: :class:`LeakageDetector` CUSUM knobs.
    """
    saved_nplc = k.nplci()
    saved_rangei = k.rangei() if rangei is not None else None
    saved_count = k.ask("SENS:AVER:COUNT?") if avg_n is not None else None
    saved_state = k.ask("SENS:AVER:STATE?") if avg_n is not None else None

    k.nplci(nplc)
    if rangei is not None:
        k.rangei(rangei)
    if avg_n is not None:
        k.write("SENS:AVER:TCON REP")
        k.write(f"SENS:AVER:COUNT {int(avg_n)}")
        k.write("SENS:AVER:STATE ON")

    try:
        yield _K2400Guard(LeakageDetector(slack=slack, H=H), k)
    finally:
        k.nplci(saved_nplc)
        if rangei is not None:
            k.rangei(saved_rangei)
        if avg_n is not None:
            k.write(f"SENS:AVER:COUNT {saved_count}")
            k.write(f"SENS:AVER:STATE {saved_state}")

from sharpelab_nb.autorange import autorange_sr830s

# --- preconditions (state this cell assumes but does not set) ---
assert_thermometry_live("T_sample", VTI.temp_logfile_candidates["T_sample"], max_age=15, max_period=12)
_T0 = T_sample(); _B0 = magnet.field()
print(f"precondition T_sample = {_T0:.3f} K (expect 1.0-1.5), B = {_B0:+.4f} T (expect |B|<0.02), "

assert abs(_B0) < 0.02, f"magnet not at zero: {_B0} T"
assert abs(k_si()) < 0.01, "Si gate not at 0"

legs = [(k_tg, TG_MAX), (k_tg, TG_MIN), (k_bg, BG_MAX), (k_bg, BG_MIN)]
n_pts, delay = 101, 1.0
I_TRIP = 1e-9   # A — hard abort threshold on either gate current

# pA-floor readback on the gate-current channels (reset at the end if no leg tripped)
k_tg.nplci(10); k_bg.nplci(10)

print(f"drive {sr1.amplitude()} V @ {sr1.frequency()} Hz -> I_bias ~ {sr1.amplitude()/100e6*1e9:.1f} nA; "
      f"sr0 sens {sr0.sensitivity()} V, sr1 sens {sr1.sensitivity()} V, tau {sr1.time_constant()} s")

tripped = []
for gate, v_end in legs:
    other = k_bg if gate is k_tg else k_tg
    mc = dict(meas_config); mc["comments"] = f"gate-current-sanity-check: {gate.name} 0 -> {v_end:+g} V, other gate 0, Si 0, B 0"
    s = sweep.AsyncStation(mc)

    s.ramp(k_tg.volt, 0); s.ramp(k_bg.volt, 0)
    xp = gate.volt

    s.fp(other.volt).fp(gate.curr).fp(other.curr).fp(T_sample)
    s.fp(sr0.X).fp(sr0.P).fp(sr1.X).fp(sr1.P)
    s.plot(xp, k_tg.curr); s.plot(xp, k_bg.curr)
    s.plot(xp, sr1.X); s.plot(xp, sr0.X)
    s.register_run_before(autorange_sr830s, (sr0, [sr1]))

    def leak_guard(station, data, _gate=gate):
        i_g, i_o = abs(float(data[3])), abs(float(data[4]))
        if i_g > I_TRIP or i_o > I_TRIP:
            print(f"LEAK TRIP on {_gate.name} leg at V = {float(data[1]):+.3f} V: |I_swept| = {i_g:.3e}, |I_other| = {i_o:.3e} A")
            tripped.append((_gate.name, float(data[1]), i_g, i_o))
            station.interrupt_requested = True
    s.register_run_after(leak_guard, ())

    try:
        s.sweep(gate.volt, np.linspace(0, v_end, n_pts), delay=delay)
    finally:
        s.ramp(gate.volt, 0)
    if tripped:
        break

if tripped:
    print("STOP — a leg tripped the leakage guard; nplci left at 10, gates parked at 0:", tripped)
else:
    k_tg.nplci(1); k_bg.nplci(1)
    print("all four legs ran without a leakage trip; nplci reset to 1")
    print("k_tg.volt validator:", k_tg.volt.vals, "| k_bg.volt validator:", k_bg.volt.vals)

"""Gate C read: four gate-current-sanity-check legs (runs 0-3). Raw R = (sr1_X/gain)/I_drain per point."""
import numpy as np, matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from hera.analysis import open_run, summarize_run, resolve_channels

runs = [open_run(f"data/{i}") for i in range(4)]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(11, 7))
for r in runs:
    print(summarize_run(r)); print("tags:", r.tags, "| interrupted:", r.interrupted)
    ch = {c.cid: c for c in resolve_channels(r.meta)}
    V = r.col(r.swept_axis)
    I = r.col("sr0_X") / ch["sr0"].gain          # drain current, A (gain-divided)
    R = (r.col("sr1_X") / ch["sr1"].gain) / I     # Rxx B_1-B_2, Ohm
    i_tg, i_bg = r.col("k_2400_tg_curr"), r.col("k_2400_bg_curr")
    T = r.col("T_sample")
    gate = r.swept_axis.replace("_volt", "")
    k = np.argmax(np.abs(R))
    print(f"  {gate}: V {V[0]:+.2f}->{V[-1]:+.2f} V | R {np.abs(R).min():.0f}-{np.abs(R).max():.0f} Ohm, "
          f"max at V={V[k]:+.3f} | I_drain {I.min()*1e9:.2f}-{I.max()*1e9:.2f} nA | "
          f"I_tg {i_tg.min()*1e12:+.0f}..{i_tg.max()*1e12:+.0f} pA, I_bg {i_bg.min()*1e12:+.0f}..{i_bg.max()*1e12:+.0f} pA | "
          f"T {T.min():.3f}-{T.max():.3f} K")

    """Locate this run's ./data dir from the notebook's own location.

    cwd (the dir holding the notebook); this survives jupyter-collaboration/

    search a few levels up so loading still works if the kernel started inside

    candidates = []

        candidates.append(Path(dh[0]))
    candidates.append(Path.cwd())
    for base in candidates:

        for d in [base, *base.parents]:

            cand = d / "data"

mc["comments"] = "gatemap: TG fast -0.3..+1.0 V (66), BG slow -1.3..+1.2 V (63), B = 0, Vsi = 0, sr1 sens 20 uV"
s = sweep.AsyncStation(mc)
s.add_comment('gatemap')

s.fp(sr0.X).fp(sr0.P).fp(sr1.X).fp(sr1.P)
s.plot(k_tg.volt, sr1.X); s.plot(k_tg.volt, sr0.X)
s.plot(k_bg.volt, k_bg.curr); s.plot('time', k_tg.curr)

        station.interrupt_requested = True
s.register_run_after(leak_guard, ())

try:

finally:
    s.ramp(k_tg.volt, 0); s.ramp(k_bg.volt, 0)

## HERA — Step 1: first 0 T gatemap (`gatemap`) → CNP line + (n, D) calibration

Gate C passed (runs 0–3: alive, no leakage, Rxx 60–330 Ω). The 1D legs show **two** resistance maxima through each gate (TG −0.21 / +0.11 V; BG −0.26 / +0.14 V, position ratio ≈ 0.8 ≈ c_bg/c_tg prior) — two series regions of different intrinsic doping. The map settles whether they are parallel CNP ridges (two flake domains, same lever arms) or not, fits the ridge slope for the capacitance ratio (`cnp-and-dline-calibration`), and locates the D = 0 line. Window: TG fast over its full range [−0.3, +1.0] V at 20 mV (66 pts); BG slow [−1.3, +1.2] V at 40 mV (63 rows). Coverage trade: BG is stopped at +1.2 V rather than the +2.0 V limit — from the prior, the region-A CNP line exits the TG window at V_bg ≈ +0.1 and the D = 0 line reaches V_tg = 1.0 at V_bg ≈ 1.16, so [1.2, 2.0] is metallic electron-side at finite D only, ~35 min for nothing the calibration or the fan needs. Sensitivity fixed at 20 µV (2 kΩ full scale — ×6 over the largest peak seen; a rail along the ridge at large |D| would itself be a read). Dwell: fast_delay 1 s against τ = 0.3 s / 24 dB (≈3τ — a uniform lag on a slope read, shifts the ridge intercept by ≲ 1 step, slope untouched); slow_delay 3 s. Priced from runs 0–3 (2.1 s/pt at nplci 10 + autorange reads): ≈1.3 s/pt at nplci 1 → 4158 pts ≈ 90 min + 63 row turnarounds ≈ 5 min. Leak guard (>1 nA either gate → interrupt, gates parked) stays on. Checkpoints: first two rows (signal level, sensitivity, TG current at V_tg = 1.0), then every ~15 rows for ridge continuity — abandon if the ridges rail or the map is featureless.
EOF

"""Gatemap read (run 5): re-form R(Vtg, Vbg) from TSV, extract CNP ridge(s) per row, fit slope/intercept,
compare to the geometry prior. Works on a partial run (fan_grids keeps complete rows)."""
import sys, numpy as np, matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy.ndimage import gaussian_filter1d
from scipy.signal import find_peaks
from hera.analysis import fan_grids, resistance_grids
from sharpelab_nb.gates import stack_capacitance, calc_nD

rid = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 5
g = fan_grids(f"data/{rid}")
rg = resistance_grids(g)
R = np.abs(rg.R["sr1"])          # (nrows, nfast)
Vbg = g.slow                     # per row
Vtg = np.asarray(g.meta["fast_setpoints"][0] if isinstance(g.meta["fast_setpoints"][0], list) else g.meta["fast_setpoints"])
print(f"run {rid}: {g.nrows} complete rows x {g.nfast} fast; R {R.min():.0f}-{R.max():.0f} Ohm; Vbg {Vbg[0]:+.2f}..{Vbg[-1]:+.2f}")

c_tg = stack_capacitance([(9.5, 3)]); c_bg = stack_capacitance([(11, 3)])
print(f"geometry prior: c_bg/c_tg = {c_bg/c_tg:.3f} -> CNP slope dVtg/dVbg = {-c_bg/c_tg:.3f}")

# per-row peaks along Vtg (smoothed), up to two, excluding edge-clipped maxima
ridges = {"A": [], "B": []}
rows_used = []
for i in range(g.nrows):
    r = gaussian_filter1d(R[i], 1.0)
    pk, props = find_peaks(r, prominence=0.08 * r.max())
    pk = [p for p in pk if 1 < p < g.nfast - 2]
    if not pk:
        continue
    pk = sorted(pk, key=lambda p: -r[p])[:2]
    pk = sorted(pk)                  # lower Vtg first
    rows_used.append(i)
    for name, p in zip(("A", "B"), pk):
        ridges[name].append((Vbg[i], Vtg[p], r[p]))

fits = {}
for name, pts in ridges.items():
    if len(pts) < 4:
        print(f"ridge {name}: {len(pts)} rows — too few"); continue
    pts = np.array(pts)
    x, y = pts[:, 0], pts[:, 1]
    keep = np.ones(len(x), bool)
    for _ in range(3):
        cf = np.polyfit(x[keep], y[keep], 1)
        res = y - np.polyval(cf, x)
        sig = max(np.std(res[keep]), 0.01)
        keep = np.abs(res) < 2.5 * sig
    cf = np.polyfit(x[keep], y[keep], 1)
    res = (y - np.polyval(cf, x))[keep]
    fits[name] = cf
    n0, D0 = calc_nD(cf[1], 0.0, c_tg, c_bg)
    print(f"ridge {name}: {keep.sum()}/{len(x)} rows, Vtg = {cf[0]:+.3f}*Vbg {cf[1]:+.3f} V, rms resid {np.std(res)*1e3:.1f} mV, "
          f"Vbg range {x[keep].min():+.2f}..{x[keep].max():+.2f}; c_bg/c_tg = {-cf[0]:.3f}; n_offset(prior scale) = {-n0:+.3f}e12; "
          f"peak R {pts[:,2].min():.0f}-{pts[:,2].max():.0f} Ohm")

fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 5.5))
m = ax[0].pcolormesh(Vtg, Vbg, R, shading="nearest", cmap="viridis", vmin=0, vmax=np.percentile(R, 99))
fig.colorbar(m, ax=ax[0], label="|Rxx| B_1-B_2 (Ohm)")
ax[0].set_xlabel("V_tg (V)"); ax[0].set_ylabel("V_bg (V)"); ax[0].set_title(f"run {rid} gatemap, B = 0, T = 1.17 K")
for name, pts in ridges.items():
    if pts:
        pts = np.array(pts); ax[0].plot(pts[:, 1], pts[:, 0], "w.", ms=3)
    if name in fits:
        xx = np.array([Vbg.min(), Vbg.max()]); ax[0].plot(np.polyval(fits[name], xx), xx, "r--" if name == "A" else "m--", lw=1, label=f"ridge {name}: slope {fits[name][0]:+.2f}")
# D = 0 line from prior: c_tg Vtg = c_bg Vbg
xx = np.array([Vbg.min(), Vbg.max()]); ax[0].plot(c_bg / c_tg * xx, xx, "c:", lw=1, label="D = 0 (prior)")
ax[0].set_xlim(Vtg.min(), Vtg.max()); ax[0].set_ylim(Vbg.min(), Vbg.max()); ax[0].legend(fontsize=8, loc="upper right")
# log view
m2 = ax[1].pcolormesh(Vtg, Vbg, np.log10(R), shading="nearest", cmap="magma")
fig.colorbar(m2, ax=ax[1], label="log10 |Rxx|")
ax[1].set_xlabel("V_tg (V)"); ax[1].set_ylabel("V_bg (V)"); ax[1].set_title("log10 R")
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(f"hera_scratch/gatemap_run{rid}.png", dpi=110)
print(f"saved hera_scratch/gatemap_run{rid}.png")
